subject: SAC-B6d static global-residual scaling comparison
intent: Isolate the effect of global-residual capacity growth with static comparison policies before introducing any input-adaptive Active or local-budget rule.

baseline.rule: equal local half + equal global half

cap128.rule: preserve local-half scaling; cap only global residual at 128; do not redistribute unused budget

cap64.rule: preserve local-half scaling; cap only global residual at 64; do not redistribute unused budget
cap64.controlProperty: small/medium/large baseline residuals are 16/32/64, so cap64 changes only the oversized profile in the existing profile sequence

firstThreeProfileControl.cap64: does not change baseline local or residual budgets for 2048/32, 4096/64, or 8192/128 profiles
firstThreeProfileControl.cap128: also does not change those three baseline residual budgets
firstThreeProfileControl.interpretation: the oversized comparison can vary residual growth without rewriting the existing first-three profile policies

findings: Both static residual caps restore the desired candidate ordering in the existing oversized fixture without changing Sparse.Active or local-half scaling.

cap128 yields a slightly larger positive margin than cap64 in this fixture even though cap64 restores far more local incremental dimensions (88 versus 24). Local incremental dimensionality is therefore not a monotonic quality metric.
The capped policies leave part of Sparse.Active unreserved rather than silently reallocating it. This isolates residual suppression from capacity redistribution.

cap64 restores graph and provenance dimensions outside the residual, while cap128 leaves only text incremental; both nevertheless recover the candidate ordering. Family-level distinctness and retrieval margin are not interchangeable metrics.
The result supports treating residual scaling as an independent capacity-policy variable, but does not establish 64 or 128 as an optimal or deployable cap.

independentReconstruction.method: Independent deterministic reconstruction of current feature hashing, B1 family normalization, B2 family-local/global residual selection, signature union, similarity, and residual-containment diagnostics.
independentReconstruction.result: reproduced the baseline, cap128, and cap64 similarities and local incremental counts used by the Go regression fixtures.
independentReconstruction.limitation: Not an exact repository Go 1.25 execution.

stopLines: unused winner budget != wasted semantic capacity
one oversized synthetic recovery != real-workload generalization
notVerified: quality across multiple independent SUI/SEI fixtures
human-adjudicated relationship between residual scaling and meaning quality
whether static caps remain useful when input cardinality varies substantially
